title: A failure is detected on the generic fibre
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring,
and $q\ge1$. If $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,r)$ holds universally for every
$r\le q-1$ ([sk-def-bc]: base change in all degrees $\le q-1$, after
every preliminary base change of $f$) but $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ does
not hold, then there is a counterexample over a field: a morphism
$S'\to S$ with $S'$ an affine scheme (so that $S'\to S$ is an affine
morphism when $S$ is separated), the base change
$f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$, a field $K$ with a morphism
$g:\Spec K\to S'$, the Cartesian square of $f'$ along $g$ with
$Y=X'\times_{S'}\Spec K$, $h:Y\to X'$, $e:Y\to\Spec K$, and a sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $(\Spec K)_{\Et}$ with
$f'^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ not an
isomorphism.

The hypothesis in degrees $\le q-1$ has to be the universal one: the
closed–open step of the proof applies it to a base change of $f$.

proof.text: We will apply the abelian-sheaf stalk and covering criteria to underlying sheaves of the actual module-sheaf arrows. This passage does not require base change for arbitrary abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients], For is exact, commutes with inverse image, and identifies the derived exchange arrows and their degree-q homology under forgetting coefficients. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves are the sectionwise kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; forgetting gives the same abelian sheaves. The geometric stalk is the filtered colimit over the same pointed neighbourhoods [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], with action λ[s]=[λs], so its underlying group is the abelian stalk. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] give exactness and detection of isomorphisms for these module arrows as well. A bijective linear map has a linear inverse: apply the map to the two candidate expressions for the inverse of λv. The same sectionwise calculation shows that For reflects isomorphisms. These observations also permit the use of the abelian etale-locality lemma of step 2 on a forgotten module arrow.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: Negate BC(f,Λ,q) using [sk-def-bc] to obtain a qcqs morphism g:T→S and a module sheaf F whose degree-q base-change arrow fails. Cover S by affine opens V_i; the opens U_i=X×_S V_i form an (open, hence etale) covering of X with U_i→S factoring through the etale V_i→S. For each i form the restricted square of f_i:U_i→V_i along g_i:V_i×_S T→V_i with the restricted coefficient F_i. If all these restricted degree-q arrows were isomorphisms, clause (3) of [sbc-lem-etale-locality] (Stacks 0EZR), applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of F as justified in step 1 (forgetting identifies the module and abelian base-change arrows and reflects isomorphisms), would make the original arrow an isomorphism. Choose a failing affine open and replace S,X,T,F by S',X×_S S',T×_S S', and the restricted coefficient. The lower-degree universal hypotheses persist, since a further base change is again a base change of f. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3),(2), g remains qcqs and T is now a qcqs scheme. All maps U→S' from qcqs U are qcqs by (1). Write p:X'→S' for the resulting base change; use S' for this fixed affine base throughout the remaining argument.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-module-bc-injectivity] (1) with the universal degree-(q−1) hypothesis. The failing arrow is monic. The exact and conservative geometric stalk criteria of step 1 show that a stalk map is injective but not surjective; choose its geometric point x and an element ξ of the target outside its image. Use [def-sbc-canonical-base-change-stalk-transitions] to write A(U), B(U), b_U, r_φ and t_U for the canonical square over each U→T. Take the original failing square to be the canonical fibre product; the identity pullback comparison then identifies t_T with the identity. Define P(U→T) by t_U(ξ)∉im(b_U), for qcqs U. Hence P(T). The inverse image of F supplies the coefficient on every U; no new coefficient ring or torsion assumption is introduced.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: For a thickening i:U→V over T, [lem-sbc-source-transition-thickening] and [lem-sbc-target-transition-thickening] give isomorphisms on the source and target stalks, respectively; the target fibre square is Cartesian by its construction. Here is the compatibility calculation r_i b_V=b_U s. The base-change mate is the one in [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Work first with derived functors, writing u^* and Ru_* and suppressing the canonical composition isomorphisms; take degree-q cohomology and the fixed stalk afterwards. Write g_V:V→S', a:X'×_{S'}U→X'×_{S'}V, and F_V for the coefficient on V. The transitions are the adjunction-unit transitions of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions]. Under the adjunction for h_U, and the identification h_U^*p^*=e_U^*i^*g_V^*, the transpose of r_i b_V is e_U^*i^*ε_{g_V}(F_V). The transpose of b_U s is e_U^* of the composite ε_i(i^*F_V) ∘ i^*ε_{g_V}(Ri_*i^*F_V) ∘ i^*g_V^*Rg_{V,*}(η_i(F_V)). Naturality of ε_{g_V} rewrites its last two factors as i^*η_i(F_V) ∘ i^*ε_{g_V}(F_V). The triangular identity ε_i(i^*F_V) ∘ i^*η_i(F_V)=1 therefore gives the same transpose. These are precisely the mate and transition formulas in the two cited definitions, so equality of transposes proves the required equality; the canonical coefficient composition maps identify F_U with i^*F_V. Consequently r_i sends im(b_V) onto im(b_U), since s is surjective, and reflects membership, since r_i is injective. By [lem-sbc-stalk-transport-composition], r_i(t_V ξ)=t_U ξ. Hence P(U) iff P(V). This verifies thickening invariance without treating an equivalence of sites as an equality of categories.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: Let D:I→Over T be a small cofiltered diagram of qcqs schemes with affine transitions, with a limiting scheme cone c, and assume P(D_i) for every i. If t_cξ=b_cη, [lem-sbc-source-image-limit-descent] gives i and η_i with r_(c_i)(b_iη_i)=b_cη. By [lem-sbc-stalk-transport-composition], δ=b_iη_i−t_iξ restricts to zero at c. Apply [lem-sbc-target-limit-zero-detection] to get an arrow j→i where r_(ji)(δ)=0. Then t_jξ=r_(ji)(b_iη_i) lies in im(b_j) by [lem-sbc-target-stalk-restriction-image], contrary to P(D_j). This proves P(c). The indexing category here is small and cofiltered, the stages are qcqs, and the base S' is affine, exactly as required by both limit lemmas; in particular this covers the directed systems required by the minimal-counterexample lemma.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: Let U→T be qcqs, with a closed immersion i:Z→U and quasi-compact open complement j:V→U. Suppose P(U) holds but P(Z) and P(V) fail. Put ζ=t_Uξ. Transport composition gives r_iζ∈im(b_Z) and r_jζ∈im(b_V). By [lem-sbc-closed-open-coefficient-embedding], F_U embeds into G=j_*J⊕i_*i^*F_U, with J the chosen injective module sheaf containing j^*F_U. By [lem-sbc-open-injective-coefficient-zero], the open coefficient component of ζ is zero: its hypotheses hold since q≥1, S' is affine, U is qcqs, V is quasi-compact, and universal BC for p holds in every integer degree below q. This explicitly uses the lower-degree hypothesis after preliminary base change; it does not assert that j_* is exact. By [lem-sbc-closed-coefficient-range], the closed coefficient component lies in the base-change image for i_*i^*F_U. These statements apply to arbitrary Λ, as their statements specify, and use the same canonical stalk transitions.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: The two components make the cokernel class of the coefficient image of ζ in the base-change cokernel for G zero. Indeed, finite direct sums are preserved by the additive inverse-image, derived-direct-image, cohomology and stalk functors: applying each functor to π_aι_b=δ_ab and ι_1π_1+ι_2π_2=1 retains the biproduct equations. Naturality of the derived base-change map in the coefficient [sbc-lem-bc-naturality], followed by degree-q cohomology sheaves, identifies the component arrows with the two coefficient base-change arrows of [sk-def-bc]. Apply [lem-sbc-module-bc-injectivity] (2) to F_U↪G and the qcqs map U→S'; the original base-change cokernel embeds into the one for G. Exactness of stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], with the module interpretation proved in step 1, preserves this embedding and identifies its stalk with the cokernel of b_U. Hence ζ∈im(b_U), contrary to P(U). We have proved P(U)⇒P(V) or P(Z).

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: For U=∅ the fibre X'×_(S')U is empty. Every object of the small etale site of ∅ is empty and has an empty covering; the sheaf equalizer condition forces its sections to be the zero module. Thus its sheaf category, all its complexes, and their higher direct images are zero. Consequently B(∅)=0 and t_∅ξ=0=b_∅(0), so P(∅) fails. The identity case and the thickening, limit, closed–open and empty cases now verify all four hypotheses of [sk-lem-minimal] on the qcqs scheme T. That lemma gives a field K and φ:Spec K→T with P(Spec K). Let g_K be Spec K→T→S' and let F_K=φ^*F. Non-membership of t_(Spec K)ξ in im(b_(Spec K)) means that the degree-q map of the field square for p and F_K is not an isomorphism. This is precisely the required field datum, with affine base S'.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: If S is separated its diagonal S→S×_{Spec Z}S is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For an affine open W=Spec B⊂S write S'=Spec A. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies S'×_S W→S'×_{Spec Z}W with the pullback of that diagonal along the pair of structural maps to S. By [lem-pc-closed-subscheme-base-change-ideal-image] this pullback is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], with R=Z, its target is Spec(A⊗_Z B). The affine-chart characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore identifies S'×_S W with Spec((A⊗_Z B)/I) for an ideal I. Every inverse image of an affine open W is thus affine, so [pqf-def-affine-morphism] gives that S'→S is affine.

source.place: Tag 0F07, lemma-base-change-does-not-hold-pre, proof (adapted to arbitrary commutative module coefficients)

proof.text: For completeness, the older unit record asks also for failure only after a preliminary base change and uses Z/nZ coefficients. That formulation is realized by the same argument: negate universal degree-q BC to choose S_1→S with degree-q failure for f_(S_1); by [sk-def-bc] its universal lower-degree properties persist. Give every n-torsion abelian sheaf its unique Z/nZ-action [m]s=ms; step 1 identifies its module and abelian base-change arrows, and forgetting a Z/nZ-module sheaf again gives an n-torsion abelian sheaf. Apply steps 1–8 to that morphism and Λ=Z/nZ, obtaining an affine S'→S_1 and the field square. Compose S'→S_1→S. The universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the two pasted pullbacks with X×_S S' and its field fibre. The arrow and its failure are unchanged under those canonical identifications. Step 9 shows affineness of the composite S'→S when S is separated. Thus both the current fixed-base-failure statement and the older unit's universal-failure statement follow without identifying their hypotheses.

lean.note: Existing upstream declarations in FailureOverField.Detection and its imported FieldFailure module state the same result. `nonempty_fieldFailure` takes q ≥ 1, universal base-change in every integer degree q' < q (equivalent to q' ≤ q−1), and failure at q, and returns Nonempty (FieldFailure Λ p q). FieldFailure records the affine S', its base-change square, field K and point, Cartesian fibre square, Λ-module sheaf, and non-isomorphic degree-q map. FieldFailure.isAffineHom_a supplies the parenthetical affine-morphism conclusion when S is separated.
